[iac] Make GCP IAM role bindings authoritative (#8650)

Replace additive GCP IAM member resources in the `marin` stack with one
authoritative binding per target, role, and condition. Grant
declarations split
across deploy-target modules are coalesced so each binding owns the
complete
declared member set.

A fresh version-3 live-policy audit covered 57 targets, 197 bindings,
and 736
members with no managed-binding drift. The refresh preview contains only
the
expected 197 binding creates and 736 obsolete member deletes. The
unredacted
preview, resolved Program-first import manifest, and state-only handoff
tool are
stored in private Loom artifacts because they contain human principals.

A normal `pulumi up` is unsafe until the 197 bindings are imported and
the 736
member resources are removed from Pulumi state. The pull request should
remain
in draft until that handoff and a no-IAM-change refresh preview
complete.

Fixes #8455

[canary] Run the TPU ferry on v6e by default (#8682)

Run the scheduled TPU canary on v6e-4 and reserve that same primary
variant for the CPU launcher. v5p capacity is effectively unavailable,
and the previous v5p-first default contributed `availability:v5p-8` to a
launcher that Iris auto-pinned non-preemptible; no scaling group
satisfied both constraints.

Keep comma-separated manual TPU overrides. [PR
#8630](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8630) independently
adds the explicit `--preemptible` launcher preference and retains
on-demand fallback. Together, the two branches implement the requested
v6e-only default and preemptible launcher configuration.

The failure signature and response are recorded in [Echo incident
244](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/244).

Part of #8658

commits.author: muchanem
commits.message:
[grafana] Route hero alerts through an operator behavior (#8575)

🤖  Route Grafana alerts through one `ops` Loom profile and a trusted
operator-behavior registry. Unlabeled alerts use the `operator` channel;
the static `operator_behavior=hero` label on Hero's four critical rules
selects `operator:hero` and Hero-specific instructions. Unknown or mixed
behavior values fall back to the default, so webhook data cannot invent
a profile or channel.

The distinct channels give generic and Hero operations separate durable
coordinators while sharing the `ops` profile's four-session concurrency
pool. Every nonterminal session explicitly using `ops` consumes that
pool; an agent-launched child without `--profile` uses Loom's `default`
profile. The additional capacity leaves room for handoffs or explicit
same-profile delegation, but it does not hard-reserve capacity for Hero.

Hero alerts now provide stable discovery and live-query guidance instead
of injecting a precomputed evidence snapshot. The operator starts from
the alert's cluster, run, and job labels, follows recent `execution_uid`
values across coordinator retries, and queries current `telemetry_v1`,
exact `iris.task_state` roots, literal-prefix `iris.task_event` and
`log` rows, and deduplicated event counts. It resolves `cluster=unknown`
before treating empty results as meaningful and compares ranks/tasks to
separate a causal failure from gang-scheduling fallout without relying
on a fixed error-signature catalog.

This removes alert-path log collection, redaction, fanout ranking,
truncation, and timeout handling. Slow or partial evidence queries can
no longer delay delivery or become the operator's starting facts.

Validation: Grafana alert/bridge tests (78 passed), Loom infrastructure
tests (18 passed), and changed-file pre-commit checks pass.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[levanter] Stop nonprimary telemetry publication (#8678)

Nonzero JAX processes suppress generic tracker metrics today but still
publish step, progress, and phase rows, including periodic heartbeats.
This multiplies Levanter telemetry by the process count.

Return a named no-op telemetry tracker for nonzero processes so only
process zero publishes training telemetry. The tracker remains
discoverable as `telemetry`, while stall and NCCL publication stays on
process zero.

[grug] Add standalone H100 hero scaling ladder (#8673)

Add a standalone H100 launcher for a 791-token-per-active-parameter hero
ladder. The existing GB200 scaling ladder and small-scale ablation
launcher remain unchanged. d512 uses one eight-GPU EP8 task, and d768

11,419/11,420 optimizer steps.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Fix EP MoE edge bounds and capacity (#8610)

## Changes

- **Ragged-dot bounds:** Restore Tokamax-equivalent K-load and M/N-store
masks on non-tile-aligned Triton edge tiles.
- **Ring capacity:** Cap local ring EP capacity at the gathered
assignment count before calling `top_k`.
- **Regression coverage:** Compare EP values and gradients with a dense
MoE reference, retain the CPU-interpreter Triton trace, and verify that
GPU `auto` dispatch selects Triton.

## Context and motivation

Haliax adapted Tokamax's Triton ragged dot from bounds-aware
`block.pallas_call` to raw `pl.pallas_call`. That adaptation lost the
automatic bounds masks supplied by Tokamax's `BlockRef`. On GB200, an
N=192 projection uses a physical N tile of 256, so accesses to logical
padding corrupted values and gradients. The fix restores the Tokamax
bounds contract only for dimensions with edge tiles; aligned paths
remain unmasked. **This is a Haliax adaptation defect, not an upstream
Tokamax defect.**

Ring EP had a separate failure: its capacity-factor calculation could
produce a local capacity larger than the gathered selection pool. In the
reported configuration, capacity factor 4.0 requested `top_k(k=512)`
from 256 rows. The capacity is now limited to the number of gathered
assignments.

The dense reference covers cross-shard values and gradients for ring,
fixed all-to-all, and pooled-wave on CPU, plus supported accelerator
backends. Accelerator parity names the implementation explicitly, while
a separate dispatch test fails if GPU `implementation="auto"` falls
through to XLA.

## Validation

- **Regression proof:** At tests-only commit `dc168c4ddd`, the [full
unit workflow
failed](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/32780486622)
in CPU and TPU jobs when the ring test requested `top_k(k=8)` from four
rows.
- **Fix verification:** The [same full unit workflow
passed](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/32782477887)
after the production fixes at `df5d8b48f6`.
- **GB200 reproduction:** Across four seeds on four GB200s, ring forward
relative max error fell from 0.79–1.93 to 0.005–0.007; all gradients
became finite and remained within 0.006 of the fp32 dense reference.
- **Local checks:** Haliax tests, targeted Levanter MoE tests,
diff-selected repository tests, pre-commit, and Pyrefly passed.
- **Coverage limits:** Stock GB200 `main` segfaults inside XLA's ragged
all-to-all before parity can run; #8549 tracks that transport rewrite.
DeepEP still requires its external source tree and FFI build.

Fixes #8578

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Preserve bounded task outputs after completion (#8638)

Preserve files written to `$IRIS_OUTPUT_DIR` as one bounded `tar.zst`
archive per task attempt. Execution-cluster policy owns the fsspec
destination, TTL, byte and entry limits, and finalization timeout.
Production defaults resolve through `marin_temp_bucket` and reject
object destinations without a lifecycle-managed TTL prefix;
`LocalCluster` stores archives below its temporary root.

RPC workers report output finalization separately from command execution
and hold the attempt non-terminal until capture finishes. Kubernetes
tasks share an `emptyDir` with a managed uploader, reserving the
configured finalization window beyond the command deadline. Capture
errors and deadlines are recorded on the archive while the command
outcome remains unchanged.

Store output metadata in a joined `task_attempt_outputs` table with
first-result-wins persistence, carry it across federation, and expose
uploaded, empty, failed, or unavailable status through task and attempt
clients and `iris attempt describe`. The Iris documentation and
`use-iris` skill cover the environment contract, retention, limits, and
credential exposure.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
Drop unread parameters and a wasted write-mode TensorStore open (#8662)

Opening a `JaggedArrayStore` with `mode="w"` issued two TensorStore
opens per
array instead of one. The guard that skips the metadata-reuse open read
`mode_config.get("delete_existing", False)`, but `_mode_to_open_mode`
returns
`{"open_mode": ts.OpenMode(...)}`, so the key was never present and the
guard
never fired. That speculative open cannot succeed under `mode="w"`: its
spec
carries no dtype or domain, and it recursively deletes the existing
store before
raising. Reading `delete_existing` off the `OpenMode` drops write-mode
opens from
4 to 2 per store (one each for offsets and data), measured by
instrumenting
`ts.open`; modes `a` and `r` stay at 2. On a GCS cache that saves one
round trip
and one recursive delete per array, per shard, while building.

The other three changes remove parameters and an option that no callee
reads.

`ScalingGroup.scale_up` documented a `timestamp` argument "for testing"
and
ignored it; scale-up timing is recorded separately by `begin_scale_up`
and
`complete_scale_up`. Removing it also made
`Autoscaler._issue_scale_up`'s `ts`
dead, so the bounded I/O fan-out passes the bound method instead of a
lambda.
`_run_tpu_bootstrap` took a `project_id` it already reaches through its
`GcpService`, and `CloudK8sService._apply_pod` took a `name` the
manifest
carries.

`include_raw_paths` threaded through `lm_mixture_data_config`,
`step_to_lm_mixture_component`, and
`TokenizeConfigBase.as_lm_dataset_source_config`
with all three implementations, but nothing has passed `False` since the
last
caller was deleted in #6649. Only `TokenizeConfig` honored it.
`HfTokenizeConfig`
and `PretokenizedCacheDownloadConfig` accepted and ignored it, so
setting it
silently did nothing for two of the three config types. Every remaining
call site
used the default, so mixture configs are unchanged.

Zephyr's `ScatterReader` held its chunks as `(source_path, chunk_paths)`
pairs
and never read `source_path`; it now stores a flat path list and takes
the
source-shard count from the sidecars. Its docstring predated the
combined-file
scatter format, describing each entry as the files one source shard
wrote for
this reader's target shard. Every file actually holds rows for all
target shards,
and `get_frames` filters each scan down to its own.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nightshift Scout <nightshift@marin.local>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[levanter] Overlap checkpoint staging with TensorStore opens (#8647)

Start each lazy asynchronous TensorStore open for arrays this rank
writes before host staging, without awaiting it. Each admitted shard is
copied into a detached host buffer, then its write attaches to the
shared open future. Ranks with no local write leave the future unforced,
avoiding object-store database access. Open, write, and commit resolve
through a promise-backed future consumed by JAX's async checkpoint
manager, preserving commit errors and the cross-process barrier.

TensorStore database opens previously completed before host staging
inside the synchronous serializer. A slow S3 open could pause training
for more than 60 seconds even when a process's complete checkpoint share
fit within the 16 GiB staging budget. With sufficient staging capacity,
all snapshots can complete and the training thread can return while
database setup and writes remain in flight. Opens run concurrently with
staging; no staging path awaits them. Saves larger than the budget
continue waiting as commits release admission.

The unresolved-open regression holds two TensorStore opens pending while
two mutable leaves stage and serialization returns. Mutating the source
buffers before resolving the opens does not change the eventual writes.
A constrained-budget regression admits one of two leaves at a time and
verifies that both rank-owned opens start before the second staging
wait. The affected selector completed 854 tests and skipped 6; its only
load-sensitive 60-second shutdown timeout passed in 10.7 seconds when
rerun serially.

A live d1024/E384 memory soak exercised about 4.0B parameters on two
four-GPU GB200 trays. Six training steps, six periodic saves, and the
forced final save completed under `s3://hero-checkpoints/tmp/ttl=1d`.
Finelog recorded 56 staging completions, 56 commit starts, and 56 commit
finishes across eight ranks. Each rank staged 4.73–4.78 GiB against the
16 GiB budget, and the two tasks peaked at 93.8 and 106.9 GiB. Rank 0
reached the step-3 checkpoint 0.335 seconds after the step-2 commit
began and 1.862 seconds before it finished. The region-local run did not
reproduce the production S3-open tail; the unresolved-open regression
covers that sequencing. [Iris
run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Floom%2Fts-open-pr8647-d1024-e384-2tray-simplified-20260825-coord).
[Incident record](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/237).

---------

Co-authored-by: Russell Power <607207+rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: ClassicLarry
commits.message:
[grafana] Add a training run's progress efficiency to the status strip (#8623)

The training-run status strip gains a progress-efficiency tile beside
active share:
`tokens_since_start / (reference_tps * wall_since_creation)` — the
fraction of an ideal
run that held its steady token rate from creation with no downtime.
Active share sees
only downtime; progress efficiency also charges the throughput lost to
checkpoints,
evals, and steps redone after a rollback, so it is the stricter "are we
on schedule"
number.

The reference rate is the mean of a sampled history of
`throughput/tokens_per_second`,
not the value in `summaryMetrics`. The summary carries only the last
step's rate, which
a checkpoint or eval step drives ~15x low (162K vs a ~2.49M norm on the
current hero);
reading that raw would swing the ratio wildly whenever the dashboard
loaded just after a
slow step. The mean over history is stable and matches the strip's
existing `AVG(tokens/s)`
tile, so the two agree.

The numerator counts only tokens this W&B run produced. Levanter derives
`throughput/total_tokens` from the global step, which restore sets to
the checkpoint's, so
a run resumed under a fresh id from a mid-schedule checkpoint logs a
nonzero cumulative
count from its first step; crediting that inherited count would push the
ratio past 100%.
The smallest cumulative-token value in the sampled history marks where
the run began and
is subtracted, carried in the same request as the reference rate.
Same-id resumes like the
hero are unaffected (baseline is one step's tokens).

Both clocks must come from W&B, not finelog: this needs the run's true
creation time and
full-run tokens, and finelog only retains a recent window (the reason
active time already
lives on this route). For hero-12d8b6f0-dee637 it reads 0.65 against a
0.90 active share.

Supersedes #8622, which auto-closed when its branch was renamed; the
Codex baseline finding
raised there is fixed in this branch.

---------

Co-authored-by: ClassicLarry <“larry36d@gmail.com”>
